messages:
anya: Heads-up — on the int8 canary we rolled last night I'm seeing a new class of parse failures for funcalls. ~12% of requests return valid JSON on first stream chunk but then the retry logic appends a mangled tail and the overall string fails strict-JSON checks.

miguel: Can you paste an example output? Is this during streaming or post-stream retries?

anya: Streaming + our client-side retry. Example:
```
{"action": "open_file", "path": "/src/main.py"}garbage--REQUEST-RETRY--{"action": "noop"}
```
So the model produced a valid object then, when the request retried, the second stream appended another object without a separator. Strict parser chokes.

eva: ugh. Looks like the retry replays the trailing tokens rather than starting a fresh packet. Is the retry reusing the same stream id?

jamal: We saw something like this with an old streaming encoder bug — duplicate tail when the KV cache offset changed. But this one only shows up on the int8 canary, not on fp16 baseline. Could be quantized LM output fragmentation.

anya: Ran a quick canary: 1k calls via mirror replica. Parse success rate: fp16 baseline 98.3%, int8 canary 86.7%. Most failures have pattern: valid JSON, then immediate ASCII suffix that starts with non-whitespace or another JSON object.

miguel: Possible mitigations: (1) shrink retry window so we don't append mid-object; (2) add a streaming sentinel we ask model to emit at end like `###END_JSON###`; (3) postprocess: extract first balanced JSON object and ignore trailing.

eva: For quick triage, postprocess is easiest. But long-term we should understand why the retry concatenates instead of replacing. @deploy-bot can you show the retry log for one failed trace?

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: replicate request id 02c9a7 - original stream ended at offset 473, retry started at offset 470, retried chunk appended to same SSE stream. See logs at https://internal/logs/02c9a7

jamal: That log confirms overlap. Retry started while server still streaming final tokens and appended its chunk to the same connection. Looks like server-side attempt to rehydrate closed connection didn't drain buffer.

anya: Filed a short-term patch: on client side we run a sanitizer that finds the first top-level JSON object and discards everything after the matching brace. Will push to canary tomorrow and re-run.

miguel: One gotcha: extracting first object can hide genuine multi-object outputs (some tools return arrays or multiple objects). Need to gate by route/schema — only apply on toolcall routes where we expect single object.

eva: Also tests: add unit test where model emits `}{` or `}\n{` across retry boundary. Exercise the sanitizer.

jamal: For root cause, can we repro locally by toggling simulated network jitter + int8 model? If quantized decoder emits partial token sequences differently, the server might consider stream closed and then reattach.

anya: I ran local repro with `tc qdisc` adding 150ms jitter + enable int8 sampling; reproduced 78/100 failing exactly same pattern. With fp16 under same conditions only 2/100 failed.

miguel: Good repro. Next steps: 1) client sanitizer gate by route, 2) server: make retry create new SSE connection rather than appending if previous stream had a completed top-level object, 3) ML: check quantized decode grouping — maybe adjust sampling temperature or EOS handling in int8 kernel.

eva: I'll file ML ticket to check decoder EOS emission probability and whether quantization affects tokenization around punctuation. Assign to @jamal and @anya for infra + client fixes.

anya: Thanks. For now I'll push the sanitizer to canary and report metrics tomorrow. Quick note: sanitizer improved parse success on canary from 86.7% -> 95.4% in a 500-call smoke. Not perfect, but buys us time.

miguel: Awesome. Leave the ticket open for root cause; label `severity:medium` and `area:streaming,quantization,toolcalls`.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary build 2026.03.21-467 deployed to int8-group. Smoke harness queued (500 calls).
